import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Handle potential missing values in 'Income'
# For visualization, dropping rows with missing income is a common approach
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Calculate total spending for each customer
mnt_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col.startswith('Mnt')]
df['TotalMnt'] = df[mnt_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Income',
    y='TotalMnt',
    hue='Education',
    alpha=0.7, # Use transparency to better visualize overlapping points
    s=50 # Adjust marker size
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Customer Total Spending vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Amount Spent', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with data
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Add a grid for better readability
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/title from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
